seams.role: TRANSPORT / INTAKE (server) — begins at HTTP, ends at wizard.ask()
seams.detail: POST /v1/ask is the only turn entry. Order: 404 route guard (705-708) -> bearer auth (709-712) -> concurrency cap inFlight>=maxConcurrent(4) 429 (713-716) -> readJson 128KB cap (720, readJson:286-311) -> validateAskBody (720, def 313-355) -> resetSessions (722, def 517-535) -> per-player cooldown 1500ms 429 (723-729) -> wizard.ask (731-734) -> telemetry strip (736) -> interaction log with redactedPreferenceResult (737-741) -> sendJson (742). Sibling entries: /v1/action-result 682-704, /v1/feedback 646-681, /v1/preferences 619-631, DELETE /v1/session 632-645, /v1/server-commands 549-574, /v1/locate 575-600, /v1/server-control 601-618. An orchestrator can be inserted BEHIND wizard.ask without touching this file at all — server.mjs only depends on the {answer, action, goal, sources, mode, kind, label, title, preferences, telemetry} response shape.

seams.role: WORLD-STATE INTAKE (the evaluator's only ground truth)
seams.detail: The live snapshot is sanitized here and nowhere else. Produces {dimension, weather, timeOfDay, player, buildState, nearbyBlocks<=16, nearbyEntities<=12, lastStructure{kind,title,dimensions,materials,features,primitives,entities,verifiedInhabitants,relativeOrigin}, lastProject}. lastStructure only survives when kind AND dimensions are both present (240). This object is the sole observation channel for the post-execution evaluator (wizard.mjs:3549 observedStructureSatisfiesAction) and for historyWithObservedStructure (wizard.mjs:611).

seams.role: TURN LOOP / DE FACTO ORCHESTRATOR — the whole body of ask()
seams.detail: One straight-line async function, no loop, no role objects. Phase boundaries (all inside one lexical scope, sharing `let answer / let selectedAction / let responseMode / let providerGoal / let contractCaveat`): (a) 4816-4835 normalizeActionRequest + player-preference short-circuit (returns early, never plans); (b) 4843-4846 bare-confirmation binding via boundPendingOffer; (c) 4847-4848 sessions.reserve -> requestSequence; (d) 4849-4884 mode classification (tuning, playerPreferences, answerOnlyRequest, reviewRequest, recipeRequest, actionHistory=historyWithObservedStructure, satisfied, instantAnswer, projectFeedback, buildRequest, conversational, retrievalQuery); (e) 4878-4881 corpus.search + relevance floor; (f) 4882-4883 DETERMINISTIC PLANNER (classifyAction); (g) 4884-4905 LEARNED-RECIPE PLANNER; (h) 4906-4923 baseline answer + responseMode; (i) 4924-4949 askModel decision + gateTrace init; (j) 4950-5166 PROVIDER PLANNER + inline EVALUATOR + REPAIR, wrapped in one try/catch whose catch (5156-5166) is the universal offline fallback; (k) 5170-5203 post-planner normalization and the guaranteed build floor; (l) 5204-5215 preference application; (m) 5216-5226 caveat + command-safety scrub; (n) 5227-5257 memory notice, sources, safeRequestId, goalForTurn, goalId resolution; (o) 5258-5298 supersede check + persistence; (p) 5299-5316 response. THE HOLE: (j)+(k) only run their contract evaluation when buildRequest is true (5097, 5174, 5179). A non-build actionable turn ("clear a 50x50 area") that the provider refuses reaches only the #44 ladder at 5074-5085 and, if classifyAction returns null there, throws into the offline catch — never evaluated, never floored.

Ordered first-match cascade, each rung a pure (question, history) -> action|null: isPotionRainRequest(1906) -> trustedAdminAction(1909, def 1636) -> localTravelAction(1911, def 1553; can return the INVALID_LOCAL_TRAVEL sentinel at 1551 which HARD-STOPS the ladder at 1912) -> commandAction(1914, def 1605) -> netherPortalAction(1916, def 1743) -> areaTorchAction(1918, def 1661) -> dimensionTravelAction(1920, def 1513) -> refusesBuild bail (1922) -> pending-offer resume (1923-1928) -> worldControlAction(1929) -> simpleBlockPlacementAction(1931) -> giveItemsAction(1933) -> recipeAction(1935) -> wool/chicken/calculator/t-flip-flop blueprints (1937-1970) -> commonFarmAction(1971) -> structureAction(1976, def 1231). Returns null for anything unmatched — this null is the single biggest source of "do nothing" when the provider also refuses.

askProvider builds the prompt (system prompt 27-49 + wizardSkillPrompt from skills.mjs:330 + conditional MC_WIZARD_ACTION_REQUIRED 4175-4177 / MC_WIZARD_GOAL_REVIEW 4178-4180 / MC_WIZARD_RESEARCH_REQUIRED 4181-4183), history summary providerHistorySummary(4104, budget 14000 chars for wizard turns), live snapshot, preference policy, sources. Transport: 2 attempts for planning turns, 1 otherwise (4207-4232); timeout providerTimeoutMs (4143-4149; 75s planning / 60s otherwise unless AI_TIMEOUT_MS). wizardEnvelope is the ONLY place model JSON becomes a candidate action, and it always funnels through allowedWizardAction (2916) after normalizeProviderAction (2914). It returns {answer, action, goal, rawGoalPresent, rawActionLabel, rawActionRejection} — the last two are the diagnostics the repair loop consumes.

Self-contained, already extracted from ask(). Up to MC_WIZARD_REPAIR_ROUNDS (default 2, clamped 1-4, line 3671) provider consults under a cumulative MC_WIZARD_REPAIR_BUDGET_MS wall clock (default 90s, 3676, checked 3684-3688). Each round appends a synthetic failed turn carrying plannerRepairDetail (3689-3698) so violations accumulate in history. Accepts only when researchAllowed && providerActionMatchesRequest && actionCompletesBuildRequest all pass (3710-3722). Returns {accepted, action, answer, goal, contract} or {accepted:false, finalDetail, rawActionLabel, rawActionRejection}. This is the closest existing thing to an orchestrator sub-loop and is the cleanest model for a real one.

Cascade: commonFarmAction (3787) -> projectFeedbackFallback (3789-3792, def 3805) -> stagedMachineProgressAction for functional builds (3793, def 3851) -> structureAction for known STRUCTURE_DEFAULTS/REPRESENTATIONAL_DEFAULTS kinds (3794-3798) -> stagedBuildProgressAction only as a CONTINUATION of prior staged progress (3801, guard priorStagedStructureProgress 3771) -> proceduralStructureAction (3802, def 3746) as the terminal always-something path via composeStructurePlan. Called from exactly two sites: 5136 (after repair exhaustion) and 5181 (when buildRequest && !selectedAction). Both sites are gated on buildRequest — this floor is unreachable for terrain/clear/level/administrative requests, which is precisely the live failure.

recipeLookup only when buildRequest && !projectFeedback (4884). recipes.find exact (4885-4886) then recipes.findBest near-miss (4890-4891). A verified entry (tier!=='provisional', or similarity>=0.8 with tier==='verified', 4892-4894) is replayed only after passing allowedWizardAction + providerActionMatchesRequest + actionCompletesBuildRequest (4895-4899). Provisional entries become provisionalRecipeAction (4900-4905), which outranks the corner guide at both floor sites (5136, 5181). A learnedAction suppresses the provider entirely (askModel at 4931).

Layered, all inside ask(): (1) researchAllowed = !researchRequired || safeNovelAction (4989); (2) intentAllowed = providerActionMatchesRequest (4990-4992, def 3405); (3) rejection recording + selectedAction=null (4993-5007); (4) prose-salvage / informational-repair branch (5008-5059); (5) recipe-request override (5061-5070); (6) #44 promise-or-refusal recovery ladder (5074-5085); (7) review gate (5086-5096); (8) BUILD CONTRACT actionCompletesBuildRequest (5097-5099, def 2984) with tri-state true / {warning} / false, then deterministic-plan adoption (5107-5115), repair (5117-5131), fallback (5136-5146); (9) accept-with-warning downgrade of a 'complete' goal to 'active' (5149-5154); (10) canonicalizeGeneratedPlanKind (5171-5173); (11) actionAdvancesBuildRequest final check that can null the action (5174-5178); (12) the floor (5179-5194); (13) final contract caveat recompute (5198-5203).

Only runs when the pack reports a terminal status. Order: unknown-status fail-closed (4634-4637) -> terminal-result replay cache (4639-4650, def stores at 4651-4661) -> sessions.updateAction (4663) -> abandonment filter (4665-4666) -> recover-existing-completion (4672-4691) / recover-existing-replan (4692-4711) -> isCurrent + newerProject supersede checks (4712-4718) -> activeWizardGoal (4719-4720) -> completed/partial branch (4721-4784): MAX_AUTOMATIC_GOAL_ACTIONS=6 cap (4728-4732), executor-verified short-circuit (4726-4727 via EXECUTOR_VERIFIED_ACTION_TYPES 3465), local world verification observedStructureSatisfiesAction (4733, def 3549), else a re-entrant api.ask with goalReview (4760-4769) whose result becomes review and possibly replan (4770), plus the staged-progress retry (4771-4782) -> failed branch (4785-4802): RETRYABLE_ACTION_TYPES (3470), failures>=3 cap (4786-4788), originalGoalContract (4789, def 3479), re-entrant api.ask with failureRetry (4791-4798). NOTE: this is the ONLY evaluator that closes a loop, and it is unreachable unless something executed.

sessions.recordFeedback binding (4451-4453) -> pending/duplicate short-circuits (4470-4473) -> goalVerified detection (4477-4481) -> forgetRejectedRecipe (4482-4495) / rememberSuccessfulRecipe (4496-4512) -> no-note branch (4513-4530) -> requestsChange detection (4532-4534) -> promotion before the change branch (4538) -> four re-entrant api.ask paths: immediateCorrection with goalRetry (4552-4568), project refinement with goalRetry (4570-4590), corrective new action (4594-4609), and answerOnly refinement (4610-4622). Each returns followUp: stripTelemetry(...).

general-mode short-circuit (6218-6221) -> receivePlayerPreferences (6222) -> bringWizardTo (6226) -> speak(answer) (6227-6229) -> registerActionRequest (6232, def 6212->414) -> preference/consent guards (6233-6238) -> a 17-arm if/else on action.type+id+version (6239-6310) -> unknown-type fail-closed (6311-6314) -> queueFeedback when there is no action (6315-6321). Each arm is the self-repairing executor (buildStructure, buildMachinePlan, executeCapabilityProgram, buildInteractiveBlueprint, ...). Nothing here re-validates the action against the request; it trusts the brain's allowlist.

Posts {player, playerId, requestId, status, detail(<=1600), context:liveWorldSnapshot} to /v1/action-result with 3 retries (313, 404-410). It then INTERPRETS the brain's reply and drives the next hop: abandonment/superseded bail (333-335), not-updated (336-339), review complete -> speak + queueFeedback (340-347), reviewLimitReached/retryLimitReached (348-355), executableReplan -> applyResponse re-entry (356-382), retry -> scheduleActionResultRetry -> askBackend re-entry (383-390, def 288-305), reviewDeferred/active-goal (391-395), failed (396-401), else queueFeedback (402). This is the second half of the orchestrator and it lives in the pack.

seams.role: DOER-side turn initiation and planning retry
seams.detail: Token/sequence guard (6329-6332), staged 'still working' chatter at 80/240/500/780 ticks (6346-6357), body assembly incl. liveWorldSnapshot (6361-6370), 4 attempts on 429 (6372-6384), THIRD ORCHESTRATOR LOOP: retryPlanning when mode==='planning-deferred' && !action && goal.status==='active' && planningAttempt<2 (6390-6394, re-dispatch 6415-6421). Stale/left-player responses post a synthetic failed action-result (6403-6404, 6410-6411).

Synthesizes a virtual completed build_structure turn from context.lastStructure and appends it to the history used by every classifier and planner in the turn (actionHistory). It refuses to do so while a prior structure turn is pending/started (615). This is the single place the world snapshot becomes planner-visible state, and it is a clean seam for an orchestrator to own as 'observation'.

goalForTurn is called exactly once, at 5240-5248, after the action is final. It reconciles providerGoal, the existing active goal, and a per-action-type defaultGoal. goalId resolution is separate and immediately after (5254-5257): goalRetry > failureRetry > goalReview > prior project goalId (for feedback/satisfied/repeated) > safeRequestId > randomUUID. An orchestrator that owns goals must preserve BOTH of these, and the requestSequence/goalId coupling used by recordActionResult (4671, 4729, 4787).

sessions.reserve at turn start (4847) claims a monotonic requestSequence; isCurrent (5272-5275) and appendIfCurrent (5290-5297) make the whole turn abortable if a newer turn started; sessions.release on append failure (5294). The turn object written at 5276-5289 is the canonical record every later role reads: {question, answer, action, goal, requestId, goalId, retryOfRequestId, status:'pending', responseMode, preferenceApplied, preferenceDependencies, requestSequence}. Any orchestrator must write exactly this shape or recordActionResult/recordFeedback/latestGoalActionTurn all break.

Zero dependency on ask() state; pure value -> value|null. It already delegates to validateCapabilityProgram (capability-program.js), normalizeRuntimeStep/runtimeProgramHasEvidence/normalizeRequesterCommand (capability-runtime.js), validateBuildStructurePlan (build-structure.js), validateMachinePlan (machine-plan.js), validateBuildPlan (build-plan.js). This is the natural 'gatekeeper' module for any new architecture — it needs no change at all.

seams.role: RESPONSE CONTRACT the pack depends on (the orchestrator's output type)
seams.detail: {answer, action, goal?, sources, mode, kind:'wizard'|'general', label, title, preferences?, preferenceApplied?, telemetry:{providerConsulted, rejections?}}. main.js consumes payload.kind (6218), payload.preferences (6222), payload.action (6231), payload.answer (6227), payload.mode==='player-memory' (6228), payload.preferenceApplied (6228), payload.requestId (6232, 6319, 6396), payload.mode==='planning-deferred' (6391), payload.goal.status (6393). Any restructure must keep every one of these fields with the same semantics.

seams.role: RE-ENTRANCY seam (the orchestrator is already recursive, informally)
seams.detail: api.ask calls itself six times with four distinct mode flags: goalRetry{goalId}, goalReview{goalId}, failureRetry{goalId,requestId}, answerOnly{originalQuestion,fallbackAnswer}. These four flags are the de facto orchestrator's message types. Each recursion re-runs the entire 500-line turn body including retrieval and classification. An explicit orchestrator would replace these six recursive calls with loop iterations — this is the single highest-leverage extraction point and it changes no validated logic.

safetyGates.mustSurvive: Every action that reaches the pack passes through this exactly once (wizardEnvelope:2916, and again defensively in 30+ call sites). It is a whitelist by type+version with per-type argument normalization; the terminal fallback (287-289) matches only registered WIZARD_SKILLS. Bypassing it lets arbitrary model JSON reach main.js's applyResponse dispatch, which does not re-validate.
Rejects \r \n \0 so one command can never smuggle a second. Breaking it allows command chaining/injection into run_commands and world.command/server.console.

normalizeRuntimeStep throws for any capability not in the 15-entry set and normalizes every argument with exactKeys()/integer()/vector() bounds (vectors clamped to +/-128 x/z, +/-64 y at :45-52; place/verify blocks capped at 400 at :127,:219; commands capped at 16 at :167,:174). Breaking it admits unknown capabilities or unbounded coordinates.

Every place/break target must have a matching verify.blocks expectation and every spawn a matching verify.entities; a world-mutating program with no verifier and no self-checking capability is rejected outright. compileBlockEvidence (skills.mjs:145-177) may SYNTHESIZE the verifier but the check is re-run at :185 — the synthesis is not an escape hatch. Breaking it lets the executor mutate the world with no proof of outcome, which also silently defeats the post-execution evaluator.

command_block, repeating_command_block, chain_command_block, structure_block, structure_void, mob_spawner, barrier, tnt are never repaired, mapped, or salvaged. The salvage path in validateBuildStructurePlan must keep treating these as hard rejects rather than droppable entries.

An explicit inert-block map (not a pattern) plus maxBlocks 128 and 8x12x20 bounds. It is an allowlist and must stay one; widening it to a denylist would admit command blocks and spawners into build_plan.
Gates which materials a researched/novel build_structure may declare. Breaking it lets a web-researched plan declare lava/redstone_block palettes outside review.

safetyGates.where: /Users/roy/Documents/mc-wizard/src/learned-recipes.mjs:40-50 with LEARNED_PROGRAM_CAPABILITIES at :14-17; applied at wizard.mjs:4989 and 3710
safetyGates.mustSurvive: When researchRequired is true, an execute_program may only use control.wait, observe.snapshot, player.break-blocks, player.move, player.place-blocks, player.use-item, script.spawn-entity, verify.blocks, verify.entities — world.command, server.console, server.configure, script.teleport, script.effect and artifact.book are excluded. The user-facing rejection text is verbatim at wizard.mjs:4994-4995: "web-researched build plans cannot contain server administration or arbitrary commands". Breaking it lets an unfamiliar-design turn escalate to server admin.

Rejects any model action that does not match what the child actually asked: review turns must pass correctiveActionContinuesGoal (3411); execute_program must pass providerPowerMatchesRequest and must not carry an unsolicited targetKind (3412-3423); build actions must pass actionCompletesBuildRequest under a real buildRequest/projectFeedback (3425-3427); run_commands, give_items, show_recipe, command_lesson, dimension_travel, local_travel, world_control each have a dedicated equality-or-match rule (3429-3461). Breaking it is exactly the 'a dragon request becomes a house' failure.

safetyGates.gate: providerPowerMatchesRequest — per-capability and per-command intent guards
safetyGates.mustSurvive: server.console/server.configure require admin vocabulary in the question (3289-3291); place/break/use/move/teleport/effect/spawn-entity/artifact.book each require matching intent words (3295-3321); server.configure settings must match the requested difficulty/gamemode/education/experiments/cheats (3322-3334); 15 guarded commands (kill, damage, fill-with-air/lava/tnt, clear, ban, kick, op, deop, allowlist, difficulty, gamemode, gamerule, reload, save, stop) each require their intent word (3335-3354); @a and @e selectors, summon targets, scoreboard, harmful effects, and large negative teleports each require corroborating request language (3381-3396). This is the densest safety surface in the codebase and it is purely (action, question) -> boolean, so it can be delegated unchanged.

Returns true / {complete:false,warning} / false. Enforces staged-progress rejection (2986), program work floors (2987-2988 via capabilityProgramAdvancesRequest:2963), project-feedback modify semantics (3001-3048), blueprint-to-question matching (3050-3059), machine kind + feedback satisfaction (3060-3066), and for build_structure: modify-mode requirement, structurePlanSatisfiesRequest, kindMatchesRequest, primitives requirement for non-generated kinds, EXACT requested dimensions (3084-3104, clamp-up only for procedural silhouettes), and authoredSubjectGeometry (3105-3113). Breaking it lets a facade/pad/miniature be shipped as a finished structure.

safetyGates.gate: structurePlanSatisfiesRequest — explicit dimensions, features, entity counts, materials
safetyGates.mustSurvive: Explicit dimensions must match exactly (raised-only tolerated solely for procedural silhouettes, 889-893); every requestedStructureFeatures entry must be present (897); every requested villager/goat/iron_golem count must match exactly, including removals (899-908); a requested material must appear in plan.materials at the right role AND in the matching primitives (910-919).

Every non-generic token of plan.kind must appear in the question or the requested kind (after singularization and synonym folding). Subject drift is explicitly never salvaged. This is the gate that makes 'a dragon request never becomes a house' true; the GENERIC_KIND_TOKENS set (3177-3182) is the only slack.

safetyGates.gate: wizardEnvelope — model prose can only become an action through the allowlist
safetyGates.mustSurvive: responseEnvelope parses JSON (2315-2325, tolerant of prefixes/fences), normalizeProviderAction reshapes (2914), and then allowedWizardAction is the only thing that produces the `action` field (2916). rawActionRejection is computed via wizardActionRejection for diagnostics only (2923). Nothing may construct an action from envelope.answer text.

It repairs supports, feature aliases, phase aliases, block aliases, primitive bounds, and re-origins geometry — but its output is still fed to allowedWizardAction at 2916, and its city branch (2838-2844) re-checks allowedWizardAction itself. If a restructure ever returns a normalized action without re-validating, the normalizer becomes a bypass.

safetyGates.gate: unusableWizardAnswer — no disclaimers, no corpus-talk, no 'ask an adult' for ordinary questions
safetyGates.mustSurvive: Rejects raw JSON, null-ish text, references to notes/sources/documentation/corpus, and 'ask an adult' on non-irreversible questions. Its failure at 4967 uses gateError so the rejection is recorded and the safe fallback answer is used.

safetyGates.gate: unsafeCommandAnswer / safeCommandRefusal — model prose never leaks slash commands
safetyGates.mustSurvive: Any answer containing a slash command when the child did not explicitly request a command, any repeating-command-block mention, or a dangerous command/broad selector even when requested, is replaced wholesale by safeCommandRefusal. This runs on the FINAL answer, after every planner and fallback, and must stay last in the pipeline.
Determines whether a command_lesson is legitimate and suppresses the deterministic effect/torch actions when the child asked to LEARN a command rather than get the result.

Exactly {objective, successCriteria, status}, control chars stripped, each <=500 chars, status in {active, complete}. Used to gate every stored goal and every review verdict (wizard.mjs:4480, 4675, 4717, 5090, 3488 via goalForTurn).

safetyGates.gate: Review verdict gate — a review must complete or correct, never drift
safetyGates.mustSurvive: A goal review is accepted only if (goal complete && no action && not reviewing staged progress) OR (goal active && the corrective action continues the SAME project). correctiveActionContinuesGoal enforces type continuity, blueprint id continuity, structurePlanPreservesPrior (3488-3499: never shrink, never drop features, never reduce entity counts), and re-checks the ORIGINAL contract turn (3529-3536). Breaking it lets a review silently replace a child's build.

safetyGates.gate: answerOnly gate — feedback re-answers can never carry an action
safetyGates.mustSurvive: If an answer-only refinement returns any action, any non-'none' raw action label, any goal, or prose that promises action, the whole provider result is discarded. This keeps honest knowledge gaps from turning into phantom builds.

An answer that promises OR refuses action while carrying no executable action re-runs classifyAction and, failing that, THROWS into the offline fallback. It must never ship the promise/refusal text verbatim. Note the exclusion at 5076 (`!(buildRequest && providerActionRejection)`) which hands build turns to the build-contract path instead.
On a recipe request the model may only produce show_recipe; any other action is dropped and the local answer used. Prevents 'how do I craft a hopper' becoming a build.

A bare 'yes' binds only to a concrete pending offer whose clause resolves to a real action or names a buildable subject; a capability menu explicitly never binds (141-142), producing one clarification instead of an unrequested build.

A player may only see their own notes; any turn with preferenceApplied has its answer replaced by '[private player preference applied]' and its preferences stripped before logging, recursively through replan/review/followUp. providerTurnSummary also substitutes 'Private preferences were applied for this turn.' (wizard.mjs:4092, 4098) so preferences never enter another turn's prompt.

A preference change bumps the session sequence and neutralizes pending/started actions and their active goals BEFORE the preference write is awaited (4360-4362), so an in-flight reply cannot be published with revoked instructions.
Prefers the opaque bedrock playerId over the display name. All session, terminal-result-cache, and preference keys derive from it. Breaking it cross-contaminates children's histories and preferences.

timingSafeEqual with length pre-check; a default or <24-char token is refused on any non-loopback host (760-762); WIZARD_SALT below 24 chars or equal to the placeholder is ignored with a warning (764-769) and a token-derived or random salt is used instead.

safetyGates.gate: Completed action results require a fresh world snapshot
safetyGates.mustSurvive: status==='completed' without a valid context is a 400. Without it the post-execution evaluator would 'verify' completion against no observation.
A status this build does not recognize (pack/server version skew) is rewritten to 'failed' with a descriptive detail — never treated as silent success.

reserve/isCurrent/appendIfCurrent/release guarantee that a superseded turn never appends a turn or ships an action, and recordActionResult refuses to replan for a turn a newer project has overtaken. Breaking it lets two concurrent child requests interleave builds.

safetyGates.where: /Users/roy/Documents/mc-wizard/src/wizard.mjs:4325 (terminalActionResults Map), 4639-4650, 4651-4661 (remember, capped at 256), 4438-4440 (cleared on session reset)
safetyGates.mustSurvive: A replayed terminal report returns the cached decision with replayed:true instead of triggering a second replan/review — otherwise the pack's 3-attempt retry loop (main.js:313) can double-build.
telemetry.{providerConsulted, rejections} is logged and stripped before the response reaches the pack, and stripped again from nested followUp/review/replan payloads.

safetyGates.gate: askModel cost gate — no provider call for canned turns
safetyGates.mustSurvive: provider.enabled && aiEnabled && !learnedAction && !((instantAnswer||groundedAnswer) && (!actionable||satisfied)) && (answerOnly||review||!action||wantsModelAuthoredStructure||(buildRequest&&hasUnmatchedDescriptors)). This is the constraint 'no new per-turn provider cost for a greeting or "build a t flip flop"'. Any orchestrator that consults a model on every turn violates it; the zero-residue canned path must remain provider-free.

safetyGates.gate: Pack-side teleport consent and broad-relocation guard
safetyGates.mustSurvive: An action that could relocate a non-participant, or that moves a consent-opted-out requester without a direct travel request in THIS message, is refused in-world and reported as a failed action. This is enforced after the brain, independently.
An action type with no executor arm calls failPendingAction rather than being silently dropped, so the goal loop sees a failure instead of stalling.

A retry needs a <=500-char question, a well-formed goalId, and reason in {failed-action, staged-progress}; a replan needs an action and a regex-valid requestId; both are skipped when newer player work exists. Breaking it lets a stale automatic continuation hijack a child's newer request.

safetyGates.where: /Users/roy/Documents/mc-wizard/src/wizard.mjs:3464 (MAX_AUTOMATIC_GOAL_ACTIONS=6, enforced 4728-4732), 4786-4788 (failures>=3), 3671 (repair rounds 1-4, default 2), 3676 (repair budget 90s), 4207 (2 provider attempts on planning turns); /Users/roy/Documents/mc-wizard/bedrock/behavior_packs/mc_wizard/scripts/main.js:6394 (planningAttempt<2), 6372-6384 (4 x 429 retries), 313 (3 action-result attempts)
safetyGates.mustSurvive: These are the only things bounding the multi-hop loop. An orchestrator that adds its own loop must fold into these budgets, not stack on top of them, or a child waits minutes and the provider bill multiplies.
The 1600-char detail cap is explicitly coupled to the pack's slice; changing one side deterministically 400s the pack's terminal partial/failed reports.

stateOwned: sessions store (src/sessions.mjs:213-310 memory, :312+ file) — the turn-history array per (mode, sessionIdentity). Mutated by: ask() via sessions.reserve (wizard.mjs:4847), appendIfCurrent/append/set (5290-5298); recordActionResult via sessions.updateAction (4663) and the review-turn append (4755-4756); recordFeedback via sessions.recordFeedback (4451); preferenceResult via sessions.invalidate + sessions.set (4338, 4362); server.mjs resetSessions via wizard.clearSession (517-535, 4435-4442).

requestSequence / sequence high-water mark per session (sessions.mjs:215 sequences Map; reserve:230-233, invalidate:234-239, release:240-245, isCurrent:246-248). Mutated by ask() start (4847), ask() failure path (5294), preference changes (4338), and session delete (302-308). This is the concurrency clock the whole turn depends on.

Per-turn goal state — the goal object and goalId. risks: THE STRUCTURAL HOLE IS NARROWER THAN 'no evaluation before execution': every contract gate (5097, 5174, 5179) is guarded by `buildRequest`. isBuildRequest (wizard.mjs:1980-1994) requires explicitlyRequestsBuild / isStructureModification / isProjectFeedback / a bound confirmation / a farm-machine noun. 'clear a 50x50 area around me' matches NONE of these, and isBuildRequest also returns false outright if commandAction/areaTorchAction/etc. matched (1981-1983). So the live failure turn had buildRequest=false — the build contract, the repair loop, and the guaranteed floor were all skipped by construction, and classifyAction returned null, so the #44 ladder at 5077 threw into the offline catch. Any design that only strengthens the post-execution evaluator will not fix the reported session.

The 'never do nothing' floor is structurally build-only. localStructureFallback is called from exactly two sites (5136, 5181), both inside `if (buildRequest ...)`. There is no floor for terrain/clear/level, administrative, effect, travel, or gift requests when classifyAction returns null. Adding a general floor means inventing an action for a request no validated planner covers — the only safe primitive is run_commands, which must still pass allowedWizardAction (skills.mjs:258-262) AND providerPowerMatchesRequest's guarded-command intent table (3335-3354, where a fill-with-air command demands clear/remove/delete/destroy/erase/demolish/break/dig/excavate vocabulary in the question). A locally-authored fill action is feasible but must be routed through those two gates, not around them.

Six recursive api.ask calls (4553, 4575, 4595, 4611, 4760, 4791) mean any orchestrator loop is competing with an existing implicit one. Each recursion re-runs retrieval, classification, preference lookup, and sequence reservation. Converting them to loop iterations changes the number of sessions.reserve calls and therefore the supersede semantics — the isCurrent/appendIfCurrent tests (test/session-actions.test.mjs, test/goal-agent.test.mjs) will be the first to break.

The pack owns half the orchestrator (main.js:335-403 dispatch on review/replan/retry/reviewDeferred/limits, 6390-6421 planning-deferred retry). A brain-side orchestrator that changes which of {review, replan, retry, reviewDeferred, reviewLimitReached, retryLimitReached, superseded, updated, replayed} it emits silently changes in-world behavior with no Node-side test catching it — the bedrock scripts are only covered indirectly by test/action-lifecycle-bedrock.test.mjs and the container e2e suites, which the owner cannot run this week.

The turn body's seven shared mutables (answer/selectedAction/responseMode/providerGoal/providerActionAccepted/contractCaveat/title) are read and rewritten out of order across ~350 lines. Extracting roles requires making this state explicit; a partial extraction that leaves some phases reading the closure and others reading a passed object will produce silent divergence (most likely symptom: responseMode no longer matching the action, which the pack's planning-deferred branch at main.js:6391 keys on).

actionCompletesBuildRequest is tri-state (true | {complete:false,warning} | false) and is checked with `contract !== true && !(contract && contract.warning)` at 5100. Any role boundary that coerces it to boolean loses accept-with-warning and turns every rough-but-acceptable authored plan into a repair round plus a corner-guide fallback — a large quality regression that the existing tests may not all catch because several assert only that an action exists.

classifyAction is called re-entrantly and with a filtered history in three places (1926, 2994, 144) and is also the recovery ladder's planner (5077) and the intent oracle for provider actions (3428). Any orchestrator that memoizes or centralizes it must preserve the `history.filter((turn) => turn !== pending)` variants, or bare-confirmation handling changes.

Fallback ordering carries meaning that is easy to lose: provisionalRecipeAction outranks localStructureFallback at BOTH floor sites (5136, 5181), and stagedBuildProgressAction is only reachable as a continuation (3801 guarded by priorStagedStructureProgress:3771) — it must never be started fresh. A refactor that unifies the two floor sites must keep both orderings and the staged-only-as-continuation rule.

The askModel gate (4931-4935) is the entire cost boundary. An orchestrator that 'always consults the planner' converts every greeting, thanks, joke, and canned blueprint request into a provider call, directly violating the stated constraint. The residue detector hasUnmatchedDescriptors (2056-2090) is the intended escape valve and depends on BLUEPRINT_TRIGGER_VOCAB / BUILD_DESCRIPTOR_STOPWORDS staying in sync with the deterministic ladder.

goalId resolution (5254-5257) and requestSequence are load-bearing for recordActionResult's supersede logic (4712-4718), the completion counter (4728-4729), and the failure counter (4786-4787). An orchestrator that mints its own per-step ids will break the 6-action and 3-failure budgets and can produce unbounded automatic loops in front of a child.

historyWithObservedStructure (611) appends a synthetic turn to actionHistory but NOT to the persisted session. Several classifiers therefore see a turn that recordActionResult will never find. A restructure that persists this synthetic turn, or that passes the persisted history where actionHistory was used (or vice versa), will change isStructureModification, isProjectFeedback, and priorStructureContext behavior across many tests at once.

providerHistorySummary (4104) has a 14,000-char budget and special-cases the project turn with fullProject serialization (4088-4090, 10,000-char action JSON). Adding orchestrator-internal turns (a planner critique, an evaluator verdict) to the persisted history would consume that budget and starve the model of the actual project state — the repair loop already avoids this by keeping its failed turns local to repairPlannerAction (3678, 3700).

validateBuildStructurePlan/validateMachinePlan/validateBuildPlan throw their whole violation list as a JSON error message, which expandedViolationList (3576-3602) parses in two shapes ({dropped,warnings} and a bare array) and wizardActionRejection truncates at 2000 chars (skills.mjs:310) to match plannerRepairDetail's budget (3652) and turnDetailLimit's 2048 (4072). These three numbers are coupled; changing where rejections are produced or displayed can silently truncate the repair signal back to one violation.
